nodes.summary: For every $n$, the 3-clauses on $n$ variables correspond bijectively to the pairs $(S, q)$ of a three-element set $S$ of variables among the $n$ and a Boolean polarity $q$ on the variables of $S$: a clause is sent to its variable set together with its polarity restricted to that set.
nodes.title: Clauses as variable sets with polarity patterns

nodes.summary: If $n \ge 3$, then there is a 3-clause on $n$ variables: take the first three variables, with polarity true on them and the normalized polarity false elsewhere.
nodes.title: 3-clauses exist on at least three variables

nodes.summary: Let $A$ assign a Boolean value to every natural-number variable, and let $c$ be a 3-clause on the $n$ variables $0, \dots, n - 1$. Then the restriction of $A$ to these $n$ variables satisfies $c$ if and only if $A$ satisfies the CNF clause of $c$: the list with one literal $(i, p_i)$ for each of the three variables $i$ of $c$, where $p_i$ is the polarity that $c$ prescribes at $i$. A CNF clause is satisfied when…
nodes.title: Satisfying a clause through a restricted assignment

nodes.summary: An assignment $a$ of Boolean values to $n$ variables satisfies a 3-clause $c$ on these variables when $a$ gives at least one of the three variables of $c$ the polarity that $c$ prescribes for it.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a 3-clause

nodes.summary: A 3-clause on $n$ variables is a pair $(S, p)$ of a three-element set $S$ of variables among the $n$ and a polarity $p$ assigning a Boolean value to every variable, with $p$ equal to false at every variable outside $S$. This normalization gives each clause in the usual sense (a three-element variable set with one of $2^3$ polarity patterns) exactly one representative.
nodes.title: 3-clause

nodes.summary: The number $4.49$ is an upper threshold cutoff for random 3-SAT: for every real $r > 4.49$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor r n \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Díaz–Kirousis–Mitsche–Pérez-Giménez upper bound for random 3-SAT

nodes.summary: An assignment $a$ of Boolean values to the variables $0, \dots, n - 1$ extends to all natural-number variables by giving variable $i$ the value $a(i)$ when $i < n$ and the value false otherwise.
nodes.title: Extension of an assignment by false

nodes.summary: A formula with $m$ clauses on $n$ variables is an ordered $m$-tuple of 3-clauses on $n$ variables, that is, a function from $\{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ to the set of 3-clauses on $n$ variables.
nodes.title: Formulas of the random 3-SAT model

nodes.summary: The number $3.52$ is a lower threshold cutoff for random 3-SAT: for every real $r < 3.52$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor r n \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables (no clauses when $r < 0$) is satisfiable tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Hajiaghayi–Sorkin lower bound for random 3-SAT

nodes.summary: There is a real number $c$ that is both a lower and an upper threshold cutoff: for every real $r < c$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor r n \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$, and for every real $r > c$ this probability tends to $0$ (when $r n < 0$ the formula has no clauses).
nodes.title: Random 3-SAT threshold conjecture

nodes.summary: A real number $\rho$ is a lower threshold cutoff for random 3-SAT when, for every real $r < \rho$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor r n \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$ (when $r n < 0$ the formula has no clauses).
nodes.title: Lower threshold cutoff

nodes.summary: A real number $\rho$ is an upper threshold cutoff for random 3-SAT when, for every real $r > \rho$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor r n \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$ (when $r n < 0$ the formula has no clauses); equivalently, such a formula is unsatisfiable with probability tending to $1$.
nodes.title: Upper threshold cutoff

nodes.summary: The lower threshold is the supremum, in the real numbers, of the set of lower threshold cutoffs: the reals $\rho$ such that, for every real $r < \rho$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor rn \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables (no clauses when $rn < 0$) is satisfiable tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$. The supremum is taken to be $0$ when this set is empty or unbounded above.
nodes.title: Lower threshold of random 3-SAT

nodes.summary: For every number $n$ of variables, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $0$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable is $1$: the only such formula is the empty one, and every assignment satisfies it.
nodes.title: Satisfiability probability with no clauses

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, the satisfiability probability $p(n, m)$ is the number of satisfiable formulas with $m$ clauses on $n$ variables divided by the number of all such formulas, that is, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $m$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable. When there are no such formulas, which happens exactly when $n < 3$ and $m > 0$, the quotient is taken to be $0$; this…
nodes.title: Satisfiability probability of random 3-SAT

nodes.summary: A formula $F$ with $m$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable if and only if its CNF formula, which lists each clause of $F$ as its three literals (variable index, polarity), is satisfiable as a CNF formula: some assignment of truth values to all natural-number variable indices makes at least one literal of every clause true.
nodes.title: Random 3-SAT satisfiability agrees with CNF satisfiability

nodes.summary: A formula $F$ with $m$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable when there is an assignment $a$ of Boolean values to the $n$ variables that satisfies every clause of $F$, that is, $a$ satisfies the 3-clause $F(j)$ for every $j \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$.
nodes.title: Satisfiable 3-SAT formulas

nodes.summary: The CNF formula of a formula $F$ with $m$ clauses $F_0, \dots, F_{m-1}$ on $n$ variables is the list of the CNF clauses of $F_0, \dots, F_{m-1}$, in this order.
nodes.title: CNF formula of a random 3-SAT formula

nodes.summary: The CNF clause of a clause $c$ on $n$ variables is the list of literals $(i, b_i)$, one for each of the three variables $i$ of $c$ taken as a natural-number index, where $b_i$ is the polarity that $c$ prescribes for $i$; the literals are listed in some fixed order.
nodes.title: CNF clause of a random 3-SAT clause

nodes.summary: The upper threshold is the infimum, in the real numbers, of the set of upper threshold cutoffs: the reals $\rho$ such that, for every real $r > \rho$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor rn \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables (no clauses when $rn < 0$) is satisfiable tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$. The infimum is taken to be $0$ when this set is empty or unbounded below.
nodes.title: Upper threshold of random 3-SAT

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
